sonnet.problem: Verse 11 makes one point in two halves: hands up and Israel prevails, hands down and Amalek prevails. Card 6 already asked the first half. Card 7 just asks the inverse of the fact the baker answered one card earlier.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The question says Moses 'picks his assistant to lead the fight.' Verse 9 only has Moses tell Joshua to choose some men and go out to fight. The text never says Moses picks Joshua, or that Joshua is leading. The question adds a connection the text doesn't state.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The question says the LORD tells Moses to write 'the battle with Amalek' on a scroll. Verse 14 only says 'Write this on a scroll.' It doesn't say what 'this' is, and the card pins down a connection the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
